meta.source: AAP Safe Sleep Recommendations (2016) · AASM Duration Consensus (2016) · Chinese Pediatric Society children's sleep health guidance (reference)
meta.usage: Used by kid-journal for sleep record comparison and kid-plan for daily routine generation. Durations are recommended ranges; individual variation exists. Daytime alertness is the primary yardstick.
meta.disclaimer: Sleep guidance cannot replace professional medical advice. For persistent sleep problems, consult a pediatrician or pediatric sleep specialist.

bands.notes: Back to sleep; same room, different bed (AAP recommends at least 6 months, ideally to 1 year); firm mattress with nothing in the crib (no pillows/blankets/stuffed toys); circadian rhythm not established; on-demand feeding; night wakings are normal
Circadian rhythm emerging; fix a consistent wake-up time; a fixed bedtime routine can be introduced from 4 months; sleep regression during rolling phase is normal; 1-2 night feeds still common
Separation-anxiety sleep regression common at 8-10 months; third nap shortens and is dropped; night feeds can be gradually reduced after solids are established (follow pediatric guidance)
Separation anxiety and standing practice can disrupt settling; keep the bedtime routine fixed 20-30 min before sleep; avoid overtiredness (the more tired, the harder to fall asleep)

bands.day_naps: 2 naps at 13-15 months -> transitions to 1 midday nap (1.5-3 h) at 15-18 months
bands.wake_windows: 3-4 hours (up to 5 hours during nap transition)
bands.notes: The 2-to-1 nap transition may bring nap refusal or earlier night wakings; observe 2-4 weeks before adjusting; fix the nap time (usually after 12:30-13:00)
Separation anxiety and growing autonomy can cause bedtime battles; offer limited choices ('blue or yellow pajamas?'); do not introduce new sleep associations (rocking/nursing to sleep)

bands.day_naps: 1 nap/day, 1-1.5 h (around age 3 some children stop napping)
bands.notes: Common issues: bedtime refusal; night terrors (not nightmares, usually 1-3 h after sleep onset; do not force waking); bedtime preferably no later than 21:00
Nightmares increase with imagination development; no TV/tablet in the bedroom; >=3 h of daytime physical activity supports night sleep; limit fluids before bed during toilet training but do not force

bands.day_naps: No nap needed (optional short nap <=30 min, not after 15:00)
bands.notes: Keep schedule within +/-30 minutes; stop screens 1 h before bed; homework and activities must not eat into the sleep floor; insufficient sleep is linked to attention problems, obesity, and mood issues

principles: 6-step bedtime routine (fixed order every night, ~20-30 min): bath -> massage -> pajamas -> milk/feed (before brushing teeth) -> story -> lights out
Fix the morning wake-up time (+/-30 min) — the first lever for stabilizing the whole day's rhythm
'Same room, different bed': baby sleeps in the parents' room in a separate bed for at least 6 months, ideally to 1 year (AAP)
Back to sleep until 1 year; firm mattress fitting the frame; nothing in the crib (pillows, thick quilts, stuffed toys, bumpers) — suffocation and SIDS risk
Place in bed drowsy but awake to build self-settling; reduce rocking/nursing-to-sleep dependence
Wake windows are more reliable than the clock: overtired children fall asleep harder
No screens 1 h before bed (blue light suppresses melatonin); dark, quiet bedroom at 20-24 degrees C
On brief night wakings, wait and observe 1-2 minutes before intervening — give the child a chance to resettle
For older children, sufficient daytime outdoor activity is the best predictor of night sleep quality
When shifting schedules, move bedtime by 15 minutes every 2-3 days, step by step; avoid large one-off changes

methods.name: Ferber Method / Graduated Extinction
steps: Complete the fixed bedtime routine; place baby in bed drowsy but awake
Say goodnight and leave the room
Return to check on a planned interval schedule: first night ~3/5/10 minutes increasing; each stay <=1-2 minutes; soothe by voice and patting; do not pick up, do not feed
Every 1-2 nights, lengthen all intervals (e.g., 5/10/15 -> 10/15/20 minutes)
Apply the same interval scheme to habitual night wakings
Sleep latency and night wakings usually shorten markedly within 1-2 weeks; keep daytime schedule and routine unchanged throughout
methods.caution: Consult your pediatrician before starting; not suitable for premature or low-birth-weight infants, those with vomiting/aspiration risk, recent illness, or vaccine reactions; crying may intensify initially (extinction burst) — caregiver consistency is essential and all family members must follow the same plan; if no improvement after 2 weeks, stop and seek medical evaluation

methods.name: Chair Method (Camping Out)
steps: Complete the bedtime routine; place baby in bed awake; parent sits on a chair beside the bed until asleep
Every 2-3 nights, move the chair farther away (bedside -> middle of room -> doorway -> outside door)
Quiet soothing or soft humming allowed; no picking up, no play interaction
Once the chair is outside the door, switch to voice-only soothing for 3-5 nights
The child eventually falls asleep independently; the whole process usually takes 2-3 weeks
methods.caution: Consult your pediatrician before starting; not suitable for premature or low-birth-weight infants; long timeline — quitting midway or inconsistency is the biggest pitfall (intermittent reinforcement strengthens crying); change only one variable at a time (chair position); follow the timetable strictly

methods.name: Schedule Adjustment
steps: Keep a sleep log for 7 consecutive days (bedtime/sleep onset/night wakings/wake-up/naps)
Compare with the age-appropriate band in this file to locate the problem: wake windows too long (overtired), naps too long/too late, or bedtime mismatched to age
Anchor a fixed wake-up time first to stabilize the day's start
Adjust nap count and timing by age (e.g., drop the late-evening nap; naps end no later than 15:30)
Shift bedtime earlier or later by 15 minutes every 2-3 days toward the target
Fix the bedtime routine and sleep environment (dark room; white noise optional)
Re-evaluate after 2 stable weeks: use daytime alertness and number of night wakings as the metrics
methods.caution: Best used as the gentle first-line approach and as the prerequisite foundation for other training methods; for newborns (0-3 months), only guide rhythm — no 'training'; if frequent night wakings, snoring, apnea, or severe daytime sleepiness persist after 4 weeks, see a doctor to rule out a sleep disorder
